stem: Release of sulfur dioxide, $\text{SO}_2$, into the atmosphere causes acid rain.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain why high levels of $\text{SO}_2$ may be found in the atmosphere near power stations that burn fossil fuels.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem: The $\text{SO}_2$ released can be converted in the atmosphere into sulfuric acid, $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, by reaction with nitrogen dioxide gas, $\text{NO}_2$, and water, $\text{H}_2\text{O}$. $$\text{SO}_2 + \text{NO}_2 \rightarrow \text{NO} + \text{SO}_3$$ $$\text{SO}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$$
parts.text:
During one year, 1590 tonnes of $\text{SO}_2$ was released into the atmosphere by a fossil-fuel burning power station.

Use the equations to calculate how many tonnes of $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ were formed in the atmosphere. Assume that all of the $\text{SO}_2$ released was converted into $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Describe how $\text{NO}_2$ is also produced by these power stations.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: State one natural cause of $\text{NO}_2$ being formed in the atmosphere.

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.text: Explain why $\text{NO}_2$ can be described as a catalyst in the oxidation of atmospheric $\text{SO}_2$.
